responses.reason: Minor wording correction: SameFile proves object identity, not that no symlink was traversed. A swapped symlink resolving to the original directory can pass. Anchoring still prevents substitution with a different directory. The explicit Git concurrency boundary is acceptable.
responses.counter_proposal: Replace 'a symlink swap yields an error' with 'substitution with a different directory object is rejected; subsequent traversal remains anchored to the verified directory object'. Retain the leaf no-follow checks and race tests.

responses.reason: The restricted namespaces, correct ancestor direction, peeled tags, and fail-closed error handling resolve the authorization ambiguity.

Source-derived PEM spans and explicit omission when source inspection is unavailable close the known excerpt bypass. Implementation tests should include a single body line, context lines, and both patch sides.

The aggregate byte budgets and bounded stderr address the remaining resource issue. Test the promised cancellation responsiveness with saturated workers and stalled stdout as well as ordinary overload.
The explicit initialization exception and distinction between malformed metadata and unsupported versions resolve the protocol wording issue.
Minor: this hashes policy and file membership, not file contents. Working-file edits therefore leave the generation unchanged; the completeness wording must reflect that distinction.
responses.counter_proposal: Call this a 'policy/fileset generation'. State that working-tree contents remain live and completeness describes coverage of that membership, not an immutable content snapshot. If continuation resumes within a file, detect changes to that file before reusing its line position and require restart when changed.

responses.reason: Command-specific framing, dedicated bounded blob reads, explicit patch parsing, and field-level sanitization resolve the parsing and presentation concerns.
Diff endpoint semantics, log commit-set semantics, and rejection of ambiguous merge bases are now explicit.
The command-specific templates correct the invalid status flags while preserving the intended hardening.
Mandatory release execution with a verified pinned binary closes the validation gap. Missing prerequisites correctly fail the release job.

The amended onboarding contract resolves the major installer, completion-reporting, takeover, and prerequisite issues. Upstream packaging creates regular root-level payload entries, consistent with the extraction rule: [v0.0.21 packaging script](https://github.com/openai/tunnel-client/blob/v0.0.21/scripts/package_release_archive.sh).
Pinned hashes, restricted redirects, bounded extraction, exclusive temporary creation, and locked atomic installation provide an adequate installer design.

The states no longer assert caller identity or successful ChatGPT delivery, and onboarding completion requires a successfully served smoke-test tool call. Display 'tool discovery' only when the observed method actually concerns discovery.
Cooperative shutdown followed by acquisition of the persistent lock avoids PID-reuse signaling and simultaneous ownership. The refusal path for an unresponsive owner is correct.
The bounded prompts, missing-value follow-up, rejection of extra tokens without echoing, and terminal restoration define a usable credential-entry contract.
Git-first preflight, separately reported permissions/connectivity states, and disclosure before service starts resolve the remaining onboarding concerns.

remaining_disagreements: Minor C1' wording: descriptor identity verification does not prove that an internal symlink was never traversed.
Minor C12' clarification: the generation represents policy/fileset membership, while working-tree content remains live.
summary: Design consensus reached: no critical or major point remains open. Two minor contract clarifications remain above. This approves the design direction, not implementation correctness; code, race tests, protocol fixtures, and mandatory tunnel-client integration evidence remain for the implementation review. No files were modified or binaries downloaded.
